Cómo llega un frame a la pantalla: How a frame reaches the screen
No hay un frame entero en memoria: la pa: There is no whole frame in memory: the screen is drawn in 15 strips of 32 columns. The two cores share each strip, left half and right half, in internal RAM, while the previous one goes out to the panel by DMA.
Animación: la pantalla dividida en 15 fr: Animation: the screen split into 15 strips; each fills from the top, half by core 0 and half by core 1, then appears on the panel while the next is drawn
A cámara lenta: un frame de verdad tarda: In slow motion: a real frame takes 16.6 ms; here, 2.4 seconds. Sending a whole one costs 8.1 ms, 7.7 of them the wire itself.
La misma escena, jugada otra vez quitand: The same scene, played again taking one thing away each time. In gotico, the two moonbeams blended on the fly ate 13 ms a frame: now they come painted into the background, and the game went from 31 to 60 fps.

pinyol está pensado para hacerse con un: pinyol is meant to be used with a coding agent, such as Codex or Claude Code. The agent reads the repository's instructions, installs what is missing, follows the recipe of the look you ask for and tests the game before handing it to you.
On a Mac with Homebrew, or on Linux.

De lo más sencillo a lo más difícil. Un: From the simplest to the hardest. A clean clone of the repository, one sentence each time and no question answered: Codex read AGENTS.md, built the engine, followed the look's recipe and wrote a script that plays its game until it passed. Then each game was measured on the console, playing that script. With Codex 0.155 and gpt-6-sol, medium reasoning. (The requests were written in Spanish; here, translated.)

El motor, los ejemplos, las herramientas: The engine, the examples, the tools and this site were written talking with Claude Code: every idea was tried in the simulator, measured on the board and corrected with what the board said.
Los aspectos que lo piden (Neo Geo, CPS2: The looks that need it (Neo Geo, CPS2, 32-bit) use AI-generated images. The engine's tools cut them out, scale them to the right height, split the frames and reduce them to the console's palette. The small looks are drawn with code.
Cada ejemplo tiene un guion que lo juega: Every example has a script that plays it by itself. On the computer it compares each frame's checksum with the stored one; on the board it writes the fps of every second. Optimisations don't change a single pixel.
